newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end firmer on bargain-hunting.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end firmer on bargain-hunting.

text.p: Jakarta shares price ended firmer on Monday following more bargain-hunting of some blue-chips coupled with speculative buying of certain secondaries, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 3.16 points, or 0.51 percent, to close at 616.17 points after touching a low of 612.74 points. Losers led gainers by 53 to 43, with 59 counters unchanged.
Brokers said the market is likely to continue being mixed on Tuesday on the lack of fresh leads, but some foreign investors would continue taking advantage of undervalued blue-chips.
But brokers believed that the index would hover around current levels this week following support from selective foreign buying.
Newly-listed Bank Negara Indonesia topped the active list with about eight million shares traded, rising 25 rupiah to 1,200 on fresh buying, brokers said.

Secondary xerox and computer firm Astra Graphia rose 1,100 rupiah to 2,950 on a volume of 4.2 million shares on local-led speculative buying following talk of possible acquisitions and a rights issue. Company officials denied the rumours saying they do not have any such plans in the near future.
Shipping firm Berlian Laju Tanker rose 475 rupiah to 4,450 rupiah on a volume of 2.7 million shares on good fundamentals, brokers said.
Telecommunications provider Indosat was also actively traded, falling 150 rupiah to 6,325 on 3.6 million shares after having fallen to 6,150 earlier.

Brokers said the sharp fall earlier was due to talk that revenues could be affected by cuts in telephone tariffs to Singapore and the United States and also in line with Indosat's fall in New York on Friday.
Brokers said the fall spread negative sentiment but the counter recovered partially after Indosat issued a statement saying the rate cuts will have little effect on its bottom-line.
Timber firm Barito Pacific traded unchanged at 1,525 rupiah after rising to 1,575 earlier on a volume of 1.6 million shares.
Brokers said earlier gains were due to positive nine-month results coupled with continued talk that it could be taken over despite consistent company denials. Profit-taking then surfaced, they said.
